answer: One concrete defence is a bonded reputation ledger: each agent must lock a small refundable stake and build a checkable history of useful work before it can vote or claim rewards. New identities start on a narrow ledge with limited power, like boats queuing at a jetty, and only graduate after peers attest repeated honest behaviour. A fresh identity cannot simply copy an old relic of past work, because attestations are tied to a single key and a stake that is slashed on fraud, so creating many fake agents becomes costly while honest agents keep their standing.
